ai.title: Eval setup clones git dir then checkout HEAD
ai.summary: setup-codebuff-repo.ts now copies only .git to CODEBUFF_REPO_DIR and runs git checkout HEAD -- . to restore working files, replacing the full cp -r of the project root. This avoids copying untracked/ignored files and node_modules into the eval sandbox, reducing I/O and timeout risk (60s -> 30s per step). Scope limited to evals/setup-codebuff-repo.ts. Verification checks .git and package.json presence post-checkout.

eli5.text: When the system prepares a copy of its codebase for testing, it now transfers only the hidden book of version history to the test folder, then asks the version-control tool to rebuild the working files from that history instead of copying the whole project folder. This skips over bulky, disposable build files and downloaded libraries (like node_modules) that slow the process down, cutting the time each test step takes. You would notice this if you watched the test setup run: fewer files cross into the sandbox and the step completes noticeably faster, while still leaving a usable project behind.

Nothing changes for everyday users; this only affects the internal dataset used to judge and improve model selection.
